# glibc expf on x86-64: per-block digests over all 2^32 float32 arguments
# (docs/research/basalt-cpu-expf.md section 4).
# Measured 2026-10-18 on Compiler Explorer x86-64 executors (Xeon Platinum 8375C and 8488C, AVX-512), glibc 2.39 =
# Ubuntu 24.04 libc6 2.39-0ubuntu8.9 (libm build-id d53fcbff9f855463606b25cfbe2a2e10856ea3a7), MXCSR 0x00001f80.
# The call is the program's own `expf` (expf@GLIBC_2.27 via the PLT), which the ifunc resolves to __expf_fma
# (libm+0x7dc40) on these CPUs: the variant basalt's pool.cpp:434 runs on any FMA+AVX2 host.
# Block k (0..4095) = the 2^20 arguments whose bit patterns are k<<20 .. (k<<20)|0xfffff, in increasing bit order.
# Digest: h = 0xcbf29ce484222325; for each argument, h = (h XOR bits(expf(x))) * 0x100000001b3 mod 2^64, where
# bits() is the result's IEEE binary32 bit pattern as a uint32 (FNV-1a's step applied to whole 32-bit words).
# The other ifunc variant (__expf_sse2) has the same digest in every block except 420 and c27; see the end.
